facts.statement: Venaticosuchus is a genus of pseudosuchian archosaurs belonging to the family Ornithosuchidae.
facts.quote: taxon: Venaticosuchus

facts.statement: The genus Venaticosuchus was first described by José Bonaparte in 1971.
facts.quote: authority: Bonaparte 1971

facts.statement: Only one species, Venaticosuchus rusconii, is currently known within the genus Venaticosuchus.
facts.quote: Known from a single species, Venaticosuchus rusconii

facts.statement: Fossils of Venaticosuchus were found in the Late Triassic (Carnian) Ischigualasto Formation in northwestern Argentina.
facts.quote: Late Triassic (Carnian) Ischigualasto Formation in the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin in northwestern Argentina

facts.statement: The geological formation containing Venaticosuchus fossils was deposited approximately 230 million years ago.
facts.quote: deposited around 230 million years ago

facts.statement: The holotype specimen for Venaticosuchus is cataloged as PVL 2578.
facts.quote: This fossil material has been termed the holotype specimen PVL 2578

facts.statement: Reconstructions indicate that Venaticosuchus possessed a slow but powerful bite force.
facts.quote: Reconstructions of the jaw musculature of Venaticosuchus showed that it had a slow, strong bite

facts.statement: Venaticosuchus is believed to have been a specialized scavenger rather than a predator of live prey.
facts.quote: Venaticosuchus and other ornithosuchids were likely specialized scavengers

facts.statement: The fossil site where Venaticosuchus was found is located at Cerro Las Lajas in La Rioja province.
facts.quote: This site, located at Cerro Las Lajas in the province of La Rioja

facts.statement: The Venaticosuchus holotype was discovered in a rock layer dominated by fossils of the rhynchosaur Teyumbaita.
facts.quote: The holotype of Venaticosuchus was found at a level where the most common fossils are from a new species of the rhynchosaur Teyumbaita

facts.statement: Biostratigraphic evidence suggests the Venaticosuchus fossil layer dates between 227.94 and 227.24 million years ago.
facts.quote: Age constraints on this Teyumbaita biozone suggest that it was emplaced between around 227.94 and 227.24 Ma

facts.statement: José Bonaparte published the original description of Venaticosuchus in 1970 or 1971.
facts.quote: The original 1970/1971 description of Venaticosuchus, published by renowned Argentine paleontologist José Bonaparte

facts.statement: The generic name Venaticosuchus combines the Latin word for hunting and the Greek word for crocodile.
facts.quote: derived the generic name from the Latin venaticus, "hunting", and the Latinised Greek suchus, "crocodile"

facts.statement: The species name rusconii honors the paleontologist Carlos Rusconi Sassi, who died in 1969.
facts.quote: The specific name honoured the paleontologist Carlos Rusconi Sassi, deceased in 1969

facts.statement: Although originally thought to include a partial forelimb and osteoderms, these remains have since been lost and are considered missing.
facts.quote: It indicated that the fossil also included a partial forelimb and osteoderms (bony scutes), but these remains have not been located by modern paleontologists and are thus considered missing

facts.statement: Bones from the right side of the skull, missing since the original description, were rediscovered in 2015.
facts.quote: Bones from the right side of the skull were also considered missing until 2015, when quadratojugal, quadrate, surangular, articular, and angular bones from the right side of the skull were rediscovered

facts.statement: The rediscovered right-side skull bones were formally described in 2018 during a study on jaw biomechanics.
facts.quote: These were described in 2018 as part of a study on ornithosuchid jaw biomechanics

facts.statement: All known Venaticosuchus fossils are housed at the Instituto Miguel Lillo, National University of Tucumán.
facts.quote: All known fossil material of Venaticosuchus is stored in the vertebrate paleontology collections of the Instituto Miguel Lillo at the National University of Tucumán

facts.statement: The total body length of Venaticosuchus remains unknown because only skull and jaw fragments are preserved.
facts.quote: The total body length of Venaticosuchus is unknown, considering that only skull and jaw material is known in the present day

facts.statement: The preserved jaw of Venaticosuchus measures 26.0 centimeters in total length.
facts.quote: The jaw had a total length of 26.0 centimeters (10.2 inches)

facts.statement: Venaticosuchus had a toothless gap, or diastema, separating the toothed maxilla and premaxilla bones on the snout.
facts.quote: The side of the snout was formed by the toothed maxilla and premaxilla bones, which were separated by a toothless gap known as a diastema

facts.statement: The maxilla of Venaticosuchus contained eight large, serrated teeth, with the second tooth being the largest.
facts.quote: There were eight teeth in the maxilla; these teeth were large and serrated, with the second tooth being the largest

facts.statement: The cheek bone of Venaticosuchus featured a Y-shaped ascending process that formed the lower edge of the eye socket.
facts.quote: The jugal (cheek bone) had a Y-shaped ascending process (upward-branching bone) which defined the lower edge of the eye socket

facts.statement: The basipterygoid processes in Venaticosuchus are separated from the basitubera by a notch forming an acute angle of approximately 60 degrees.
facts.quote: The basipterygoid processes are separated from the basitubera by means of a pronounced notch which forms an acute angle (~60 degrees)

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Venaticosuchus was robust and proportionally more similar to Ornithosuchus than to Riojasuchus.
facts.quote: The mandible (lower jaw) was robust, proportionally more similar to Ornithosuchus rather than Riojasuchus

facts.statement: The first two teeth of the lower jaw were very large and overlapped the snout at the level of the upper jaw gap.
facts.quote: The first two teeth of the dentary were very large, overlapping the snout at the level of the maxillary/premaxillary diastema

facts.statement: The two enlarged lower jaw teeth of Venaticosuchus were unserrated and oval in cross-section.
facts.quote: The two enlarged dentary teeth of Venaticosuchus were unserrated and oval-shaped in cross section

facts.statement: The angular bone of the lower jaw was elongated, formed the entire lower edge of the jaw opening, and was covered with striations.
facts.quote: The angular bone (which forms the rear lower part of the mandible) was elongated, forming the entire lower edge of the mandibular fenestra and being covered with striations

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Venaticosuchus had a swollen, rough-textured area of bone on the left side of its skull that was likely caused by a facial infection.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen possessed a peculiar pathology (sign of an injury or disease) on the left side of the skull.

facts.statement: The left upper jaw of the holotype specimen was missing two tooth sockets compared to the right side, suggesting a severe injury or disease.
facts.quote: In addition, the left maxilla has only six tooth sockets (compared to eight in the right maxilla), with the last two tooth sockets missing.

facts.statement: Venaticosuchus possessed the highest combined adductor muscle moment arm value of any ornithosuchid, indicating a very powerful bite mechanism.
facts.quote: Venaticosuchus had the highest "AM" value (corresponding to the sum of all adductor muscle moment arms) of any of the ornithosuchids, though some of its muscles had lower moment arms than other reptiles sampled.

facts.statement: Venaticosuchus had a slow bite speed because its powerful jaw muscles took a long time to retract.
facts.quote: However, the high AM value also means that the muscles would take longer to retract, giving it a fairly slow bite.

facts.statement: Venaticosuchus shared a slow but strong bite with other ornithosuchids and the aetosaur Desmatosuchus, contrasting with the fast bites of modern crocodilians and basal aetosaurs.
facts.quote: This slow, strong bite is also shared by other ornithosuchids as well as the aetosaur Desmatosuchus, but contrasts with the weak, fast bite of the carnivorous basal aetosaur Neoaetosauroides and the fast, moderately strong bite of Alligator.

facts.statement: One hypothesis suggests Venaticosuchus was a specialized scavenger that used its strong bite to process carcasses.
facts.quote: Von Baczko (2018) proposed that ornithosuchids were specialized scavengers, which could deal with carcasses using their strong bite force and serrated teeth.

facts.statement: A 2023 study suggests Venaticosuchus may have been piscivorous, capturing small aquatic animals underwater and swallowing them whole, similar to a heron or Spinosaurus.
facts.quote: In a 2023 study, biomechanical analysis again found that the related Riojasuchus had poor resistance to lateral forces and greater resistance to traction and torsion forces, but it was noted that the short mandible (shorter than the upper jaw, as typical for ornithosuchids) did not allow occlusion between the mandibular teeth and those on the premaxilla.

facts.statement: The genus Venaticosuchus was named by Bonaparte in 1971.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Bonaparte, 1971

facts.statement: The only known species, Venaticosuchus rusconii, lived in Argentina during the Late Triassic, approximately 210 million years ago.
facts.quote: Solo se ha descrito a una especie de Venaticosuchus, la especie tipo, V. rusconii del Triásico Superior de Argentina, que data de alrededor de hace 210 millones de años.

facts.statement: Venaticosuchus was a medium-sized predator that could reach up to 2 meters in length.
facts.quote: Fue un depredador de tamaño mediano, que alcanzaba hasta 2 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Venaticosuchus was originally thought to be an ancestor of large theropod dinosaurs like Tyrannosaurus, but is now known to be more closely related to crocodilians.
facts.quote: Originalmente se pensó que era el antepasado de los dinosaurios carnosaurios (un grupo que se pensó abarcaba a todos los terópodos grandes, como Tyrannosaurus); sin embargo, ahora se sabe que están más estrechamente relacionados con los cocodrilos que con los dinosaurios.

facts.statement: Venaticosuchus belongs to the family Ornithosuchidae, which consisted of facultatively bipedal carnivorous crocodylomorphs widespread during the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Venaticosuchus es miembro de Ornithosuchidae, una familia de crurotarsos carnívoros facultativamente bípedos que estaban geográficamente extendidos durante el Triásico Superior.

facts.statement: The time range for Venaticosuchus is estimated to be from 233.6 to 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (233.6 to 227.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Fossils of Venaticosuchus were recovered from a single site in Argentina during the early 1960s.
rejected.quote: Fossils of Venaticosuchus have only been recovered, in the early sixties, from a single fossil site in Argentina

rejected.statement: The quadrate bone in Venaticosuchus forms a steep angle identical to that of the adjacent quadratojugal bone.
rejected.quote: The quadrate bone, which lies adjacent to the quadratojugal and forms the upper half of the jaw joint), forms a steep angle identical to that of the quadratojugal
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'forms a steep angle identical to that of'

rejected.statement: Venaticosuchus had the highest bite force of any reptile sampled in Von Baczko's 2018 study, despite having an average bite moment.
rejected.quote: Despite its average bite moment, the high AM value of Venaticosuchus gave it the highest ratio between AM and bite moment, corresponding to the highest bite force of any of the reptiles sampled.
